newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the weeks of Feb 3, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - IBM Corp, NEC Computer Systems Division and Compaq Computer Corp are all readying notebooks for the first half of 1997 that promise advanced technologies such as 12-speed CD-ROM, 13.3 inch displays and two gigabyte hard drives, PC Week reported Feb. 3.
VeriSign Inc will debut in March a major enhancement to its digital certificates that make them a secure container for storing virtually any type of data, PC Week reported Feb. 3

COMPUTERWORLD - If America Online Inc's recent network problems are the sign of things to come for Internet access providers, they could face formidable legal pressures with several states proposing legislation to slap fines on ISPs whose service levels plummet due to oversubscribing, Computerworld reported Feb. 3.

A handful of firms last week began issuing year 2000 insurance policies with limits of $100-200 million, designed to cover unforeseen business disruptions that may occur when systems are converted to handle the century date change, Computerworld reported Feb. 3.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - U.S. Robotics Corp and Rockwell International Corp, leaders of the two rival camps racing to offer 56-kilobit modem technology, face several obstacles in bringing the new higher speed Internet access systems to market, Comms Week reported Feb. 3. Besides a lack of industry standards that would make the competing systems compatible, the report questioned whether the modems actually can attain the roughly 56,000 bit per second speeds in real-world conditions.

EE TIMES - The biggest change in networking technology since the emergence of routers in the 1980s could catch fire at the ComNet 97 conference this week, in a form of a new generation of fast protocols that could boost Internet data transmission speeds 10-fold, EE Times reported Feb. 3.

In a bold move to stake out the high ground in digital signal processing, Texas Instruments Inc will introduce Monday a fixed point digital signal processor family based on unconventional very long instruction word (VLIW) architecture, EE Times reported on Feb. 3.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - The South Korean government has prodded the country's three largest chip makers to slash production of 16 megabit dynamic random access memory chips, following a year of failed attempts to halt an unrelenting drop in memory chip prices, EBN reported Feb. 3.

Hyundai Corp, LG Semicon Co Ltd and Samsung Electronics all said they will slow production of 16-megabit DRAM chips by as much as 30 percent. The companies said they cut production because prices had fallen so much that their businesses were no longer profitable and threatened their ability to invest in future products.
